not_covered: New initial orientations, weakened actuators, terrain or impacts
Robot self-collision response or continuous-time path clearance
qualification_economy: Reuse the native owner, capture, shared reader and retained-path diagnostic. Fourteen controls cover the optional handoff interface, balanced assignment, fresh reference comparison, complete inventory and required route branches. No new physical owner or native reader.
purpose: Search 36 upright-steering and support-handoff profiles across 24 bodies against fresh selected-profile, timed and brake comparators.
selection_rationale: Twenty-four configured profiles cross four signed axes, drive/rock strategies and three normal/friction/load settings. Each runs on four bodies inside and four outside the 31-body geometric pitch group. Each body receives eight proposals and two fresh unchanged comparators. Exposed geometry is proposal provenance, never held-out evidence.
braking_model_limit: Constant-velocity lookahead and a stopping-speed envelope using a declared 6 rad/s^2 shaping estimate. This is not a validated physical deceleration bound or a guarantee that no joint crosses its limit.
body_moment_limit: Clear geometric targets are not collision-free transitions. Geometric capsule low points are not measured contact locations. Friction cones and normal load are configured proposals; static joint compensation omits inertial, Coriolis, passive and limit forces. Actual force, contact and sampled work are retained. Motors, native collision filtering and eligibility remain unchanged.
code_path_risks_covered: Measured upright steering with bounded axis slew
Continuous, clock and measured-stall schedules; release, reacquisition and bounded fallback
Release toward a neutral pose without requested reaction forces
Exact full replay and same-run compact projection on the native route
Synthetic upright reset, atomic memory, guards and fresh-reference assessment controls
Prospectively required retained-sample path screen after broad native discovery
route_horizon_rationale: Six seconds covers repeated 180-step push plus 24-step release cycles and 90-step clock plus 30-step release cycles after contact acquisition; one or two steps cannot cover these late transitions. The twelve route roles cover three fresh comparators and nine variants spanning four seed axes, three biases and three schedules. Successful recovery and the upright-reset branch are not required native-route coverage.
